chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding two men: one of whom restrained [the victim], and the other killed [him]. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The killer shall be killed, and the other one shall be imprisoned until he dies of anguish, just as he held him until he died of anguish.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling when one person restrains a victim and another kills him?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) illustrates the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing between direct causation and instrumental contribution in homicide. By sentencing the restrainer to die of 'ghamm' (anxiety or grief) in confinement, the Imam emphasizes proportional retribution (ta'zir) that mirrors the specific suffering inflicted, a concept deeply rooted in the jurisprudential commentaries of al-Kulayni and later scholars like al-Majlisi.
